- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 79.16 → 82.31), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too much upward bias after recent peaks.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the 30d window.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the final 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model overreacts and forecasts even higher than true outcome.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, leading to underprediction of sharp reversals or spikes.
- Forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to recent history as horizon extends — model “smooths” out short-term noise.
